---
title: "User Guide"
---

## Thematic evolution

The module produces `data/processed/thematic/thematic_sankey.png`
and `thematic_sankey.svg`, plus analytical node/edge CSV files and an RDS object.
The static two-period diagram preserves positive lineage-strength weights; it
is not an interactive HTML chart. At least two distinct valid publication years
and usable Keywords Plus (`ID`) are required. Single-year input is logged as
`skipped`; genuine analytical or rendering errors are logged as `failed`.
These changes are included in the v2.3.2 preparation, not in archived v2.3.1.
The repeated benchmark at commit `2e7cd2854c3aef9073e30ac9e813ba2fef97ddca`
completed successfully; see the release preparation record for its scope.
SVG export uses R's Cairo graphics device. On macOS, install XQuartz if R reports
missing X11/Cairo libraries; restart R after installation. CI installs XQuartz
explicitly. Export failures remain real failures, not silently skipped images.

## RStudio setup

1. Clone the repository and open `slr-suite.Rproj` in RStudio.
2. Install `renv` once and run `renv::restore()` to recreate the dependency versions recorded in `renv.lock`. The application never installs packages during a run.
3. Place a Web of Science Plain Text export (`.txt`) in `data/raw/`. SLR Suite does not parse Scopus CSV files directly. For a mixed-source review, combine the Web of Science Plain Text export and Scopus CSV upstream with BibexPy, then place the resulting harmonized TXT file in `data/raw/`.
4. Review the YAML files in `config/` and record any protocol changes before analysis.
5. Run `source("master_launcher.R")` for the interactive menu, or use `Rscript master_launcher.R run`.

Generated analysis files belong under `data/interim/` and `data/processed/`. Execution records are written to `logs/pipeline_runs.csv`.

## Configurable screening

Edit `config/screen_criteria.yaml` to define required fields, included languages and normalized document types, optional year bounds, and exclusion patterns. The screening step writes all record-level decisions and reasons to `data/interim/screening_decisions.csv`; it does not replace independent researcher eligibility assessment.

## User dictionary

`config/tccm_dictionaries.yaml` is the single researcher-editable source of TCCM dimensions, labels, and regular-expression patterns. Keep every label under a named dimension and quote patterns containing backslashes. `R/dictionaries.R` defines the reader and structural validation rules; `scripts/config_dictionaries.R` invokes that reader and exposes the validated `dimensions` section as `TCCM_DICTIONARIES`; and `scripts/05_tccm_matrix.R` applies those dictionaries independently to each bibliographic record. The loader script does not contain a second dictionary.

For each input row, the TCCM module combines the title, abstract, author keywords, and Keywords Plus into one normalized record-level string. Each configured dimension is evaluated separately for that string. Matching labels are retained as unique semicolon-separated values, and a record with no matching pattern receives `NA`. Input and output row order is preserved, and the module verifies that the final TCCM matrix contains exactly one row for every input record.

## Validation

Run `Rscript master_launcher.R validate` before reporting results. The command writes a machine-readable checklist and session summary to `artifacts/validation/`. Run `Rscript tests/testthat.R` for automated tests.

For maintainer-level verification, also run `Rscript scripts/quality_gate.R`, `Rscript test_all.R`, and `Rscript scripts/coverage_gate.R`.

## Scope

SLR Suite automates data preparation and selected bibliometric outputs. Screening decisions, interpretation, risk-of-bias assessment, and scientific conclusions remain researcher responsibilities.
